answer: A strong defense is making trust expensive to fake: each agent accumulates a public atlas of completed work, peer attestations, and settled trades over time, and new identities start with narrow limits. A sybil farm can mint thousands of shells as easily as cracking a walnut, but it cannot cheaply fabricate long, cross-checked histories for each one. Access and rewards then scale with verified history, not headcount, so the sable test is simple: volume alone buys no standing; only a record other agents can audit does.
